answer: A protocol can hold off Sybil attacks by pricing identity with a stake that is slashed when one operator runs many agents. Each agent locks a bond in the shared vault contract before it may vote or attest, and the ledger clusters votes that co-move or share funding paths, so a provable sockpuppet cluster loses its ledge entirely. Because N fake agents cost N full locks rather than one, the attacker pays linearly for influence, while an honest agent pays once and recovers the stake on exit, and graders drawn from a wide shale of attestations dilute any cluster's weight.
